cues.en: There's a similar pattern you'll see in the skyline of cities all over The US and Canada.
cues.zh: 在美国和加拿大各地的城市天际线中，你都会看到类似的模式。

cues.en: The city is sprawling and flat, then suddenly,
cues.zh: 城市先是平坦地向外蔓延，然后突然，

cues.en: a bunch of giant towers.
cues.zh: 出现一堆巨大的高楼。

cues.en: Here it is in Minneapolis,
cues.zh: 这是明尼阿波利斯的情况，

cues.en: and in Charlotte,
cues.zh: 还有夏洛特，

cues.en: and in Seattle.
cues.zh: 以及西雅图。

cues.en: But compare that to almost any European city, and you'll get a much smoother progression of buildings with lots that are of an in between size.
cues.zh: 但把这就和几乎任何欧洲城市对比，你会看到建筑高度平滑过渡，地块大小介于两者之间。

cues.en: When I criticize American car dependent suburbs, there's a common knee jerk reaction.
cues.zh: 当我批评美国依赖汽车的郊区时，常见的本能反应是：

cues.en: Someone will inevitably claim, I live in the suburbs because I don't want to be crammed into a concrete box in the sky,
cues.zh: 总有人会说：“我住在郊区，因为我不想被塞进混凝土天空盒子里。”

cues.en: As if there's no alternative between a concrete tower and car dependent suburbia with asphalt as far as the eye can see.
cues.zh: 好像混凝土高楼和一眼望去全是沥青、依赖汽车的郊区之间没有其他选择似的。

cues.en: Now, you might just dismiss this person as being an ignorant idiot, and to be fair, they probably are. But there's a small bit of reality in that statement because in most of The US and much of Canada,
cues.zh: 你可能会直接把这个人当成无知的傻瓜，公平地说，他们大概确实是。但这句话里有一小部分现实，因为在美国大部分地区和加拿大很多地方，

cues.en: those are your only two options to live, an apartment or a single family home. There's almost nothing in between.
cues.zh: 你只有两种居住选择：公寓或独栋住宅。中间几乎没有别的。

cues.en: Urban planners have dubbed this the missing middle problem, and it affects almost every city in The US and Canada with very, very few exceptions.
cues.zh: 城市规划者把这称为“缺失的中间”问题，它影响美国和加拿大几乎所有城市，例外极少。

cues.en: As with most things wrong with urban planning in America, this all started in the nineteen forties when cities started promoting car centric suburbanization
cues.zh: 和美国城市规划的大多数问题一样，这一切始于20世纪40年代，当时城市开始推动以汽车为中心的郊区化，

cues.en: with an emphasis on every family owning their own detached home.
cues.zh: 强调每个家庭都拥有自己的独栋住宅。

cues.en: Now if single family homes were built because people wanted single family homes and the market demanded it, that might be okay, but it's not that simple.
cues.zh: 如果独栋住宅是因为人们想要独栋住宅、市场需求如此而建，那或许还可以接受，但事情没那么简单。

cues.en: Instead, it became almost impossible to build anything other than single family homes because of strict Euclidean zoning.
cues.zh: 相反，由于严格的欧几里得式分区，除了独栋住宅之外，几乎不可能建任何其他东西。

cues.en: I've referred to this before in my Livable Neighbourhoods video.
cues.zh: 我在之前的《宜居社区》视频里提到过这一点。

cues.en: And zoning is not the only problem either.
cues.zh: 而且分区并不是唯一的问题。

cues.en: There are other car centric policies, especially minimum parking requirements, that reinforce this as well.
cues.zh: 还有其他以汽车为中心的政策，尤其是最低停车位要求，也在加剧这一问题。

cues.en: All of these requirements severely constrain what can be built.
cues.zh: 所有这些要求都严重限制了可以建造什么。

cues.en: In particular, it makes it almost impossible to build the traditional walkable neighborhoods that are enjoyable, efficient, sustainable,
cues.zh: 尤其是，它让建造那些令人愉悦、高效、可持续的传统步行社区变得几乎不可能，

cues.en: and financially solvent.
cues.zh: 且在财务上不可持续。

cues.en: This problem is endemic across The US. If you look at areas of a US city where residential buildings are permitted, you find that almost all of it only allows for single family homes.
cues.zh: 这个问题在美国各地普遍存在。如果你看看美国城市中允许建住宅的区域，你会发现几乎所有这些区域都只允许建独栋住宅。

cues.en: It's illegal to build anything else.
cues.zh: 建其他任何东西都是违法的。

cues.en: The worst offender here is San Jose, where 94%
cues.zh: 最严重的是圣何塞，那里有94%

cues.en: of the land that allows building housing only permits building single family homes.
cues.zh: 的允许建住房的土地只允许建独栋住宅。

cues.en: And this is in the heart of Silicon Valley, where more housing is desperately needed.
cues.zh: 而这还是在硅谷的核心地带，那里迫切需要更多住房。

cues.en: Canadian cities are much better, but still far too high. Remember what this means is that developers must build single family homes in these areas even if there's demand for something else.
cues.zh: 加拿大城市要好得多，但仍然太高了。记住，这意味着开发商在这些区域必须建独栋住宅，即使市场对其他类型有需求。

cues.en: There's no other choice.
cues.zh: 别无选择。

cues.en: This ultimately leads to a scarcity in residential land for any other type of building. And even then, nearby residents can object to almost any development, which means that every new development is going to be a fight.
cues.zh: 这最终导致可用于其他类型建筑的住宅用地变得稀缺。即便如此，附近居民几乎可以反对任何开发项目，这意味着每个新开发项目都将是一场斗争。

cues.en: This is a major reason why developers build condo towers so often in The US and Canada.
cues.zh: 这是美国和加拿大开发商经常建造公寓高楼的一个主要原因。

cues.en: Because getting zoning approval isn't cheap or easy, and fighting NIMBYs isn't cheap or easy either.
cues.zh: 因为获得分区批准既不便宜也不容易，而应对NIMBY（邻避主义者）同样既不便宜也不容易。

cues.en: So a developer is only going to put the effort into jumping through all of these hoops if they're sure they can make a profit in the end.
cues.zh: 因此，开发商只有在确信最终能获利的情况下，才会费尽心思去跳过所有这些障碍。

cues.en: That means making the absolute most of the scarce residential land and ultimately that means cramming in as many residents as possible.
cues.zh: 这意味着要最大限度地利用稀缺的住宅用地，最终就意味着要尽可能多地塞进居民。

cues.en: Which is why you end up with this insane situation of the lowest density single family homes next to giant high rise towers in the most expensive city in Canada.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么在加拿大最昂贵的城市，你会看到低密度独栋住宅紧邻巨型高楼的疯狂局面。

cues.en: But of course, it didn't used to be this way. Consider this street in Toronto built in the nineteen twenties.
cues.zh: 但当然，过去并非如此。看看多伦多这条建于20世纪20年代的街道。

cues.en: Here you can see detached homes of various different sizes, like this cute blue house
cues.zh: 在这里你可以看到各种不同大小的独立住宅，比如这栋可爱的蓝色房子

cues.en: or this small bungalow.
cues.zh: 或者这个小平房。

cues.en: There are also several terraced homes like these.
cues.zh: 还有几栋像这样的联排住宅。

cues.en: And this looks like a single house, but it's actually several apartments in one building. But it still fits in very neatly into the neighborhood.
cues.zh: 这看起来像是一栋单独的住宅，但实际上是一栋建筑里的几套公寓。但它仍然非常整齐地融入了社区。

cues.en: Then there's this very small apartment block too.
cues.zh: 还有这个非常小的公寓楼。

cues.en: And these small terraced homes that have clearly seen better days.
cues.zh: 这些小小的联排住宅，显然已经风光不再。

cues.en: And finally, at the end of the street, there's commercial buildings like this one within easy walking distance of residence.
cues.zh: 最后，在街道尽头，有这样的商业建筑，离住宅区步行即可到达。

cues.en: And apartments were built over most of the shops as well.
cues.zh: 而且大多数商铺上面还建了公寓。

cues.en: Today, it is nearly impossible to find any place in The US or Canada where all of these different types of buildings would be legal to build on the same street, something that would be completely normal before the nineteen forties.
cues.zh: 如今，在美国或加拿大，几乎找不到任何一个地方，能让所有这些不同类型的建筑合法地建在同一条街上，而这在四十年代之前完全是稀松平常的事。

cues.en: But even if you could get the zoning variances to build this small multiunit building, which you can't, the neighbors would absolutely lose their minds.
cues.zh: 但就算你能拿到区划豁免，来建这种小型多户建筑——而你根本拿不到——邻居们也绝对会炸锅。

cues.en: We can't have people of marginally lower socioeconomic
cues.zh: 我们不能让社会经济地位稍低的人

cues.en: status in our neighborhood. And what if their skin color was different? Could you imagine?
cues.zh: 住进我们社区。要是他们的肤色还不一样呢？你能想象吗？

cues.en: So instead, we get a 40 story condo tower down the street.
cues.zh: 于是取而代之，我们在街那头得到了一栋40层的公寓塔楼。

cues.en: The situation in Europe is very different.
cues.zh: 欧洲的情况则大不相同。

cues.en: Here in The Netherlands, for example, you'll very often see mid rise buildings that are five floors or less and many terraced homes as well.
cues.zh: 比如在荷兰，你经常会看到五层以下的中层建筑，还有很多联排住宅。

cues.en: It is possible to find single family homes too, of course, but it's not the only type of housing available.
cues.zh: 当然，独栋住宅也能找到，但它并不是唯一可选的住房类型。

cues.en: This street in Dauvindrecht,
cues.zh: 这条街位于 Dauvindrecht，

cues.en: an utterly normal city near Amsterdam,
cues.zh: 一个紧邻阿姆斯特丹的再普通不过的城市，

cues.en: has terraced homes mixed with semi detached homes and small apartment buildings all in the same place.
cues.zh: 联排住宅与半独立住宅、小型公寓楼混杂在同一片区域。

cues.en: This provides so much more choice in the housing market, especially for families.
cues.zh: 这为住房市场提供了多得多的选择，尤其是对有孩子的家庭来说。

cues.en: Not everybody wants to maintain a big house with a big yard and live in a place where you have to drive to do just about anything.
cues.zh: 并不是每个人都想维护一栋带大院子的房子，也不想住在一个几乎干什么都得开车的地方。

cues.en: And it also allows for the type of enjoyable, livable, walkable urban neighborhoods that I'm constantly praising on this channel as being some of the best places in the world to live. You can even live in a concrete box in the sky, if you like that kind of thing.
cues.zh: 它也让那种宜人、宜居、适合步行的城市街区成为可能——我在这个频道里一直称赞这类地方是世界上最适合居住的地方之一。如果你喜欢，甚至可以住在空中的混凝土盒子里。

cues.en: So maybe you don't like these kind of homes, and that's okay. They don't like you either.
cues.zh: 所以也许你不喜欢这类住宅，没关系。它们也不喜欢你。

cues.en: But even if you don't like these kind of homes, you have to justify why it is illegal to build these kind of homes in almost every neighborhood in The US and Canada.
cues.zh: 但即使你不喜欢这类住宅，你也得解释清楚：为什么在美国和加拿大几乎每个街区，建这类住宅都是违法的。

cues.en: Of course, eliminating single family zoning doesn't eliminate single family homes. These houses can still be built if there's demand for it. It just means they would no longer be the only type of homes that can be built.
cues.zh: 当然，取消单户住宅分区并不等于取消独栋住宅。只要有需求，这类房子仍然可以建。它只是意味着，它们不再是唯一可以建的住宅类型。

cues.en: Thankfully, some cities in North America are starting to make some progress with this issue.
cues.zh: 所幸，北美一些城市开始在这个问题上取得进展。

cues.en: Minneapolis abolished single family zoning and now allows building duplexes and triplexes in any neighborhood in the city.
cues.zh: 明尼阿波利斯废除了单户住宅分区，现在允许在全市任何街区建造双拼和三拼住宅。

cues.en: Vancouver has recently made it possible to build duplexes in all residential neighborhoods, though not triplexes.
cues.zh: 温哥华最近允许在所有住宅街区建造双拼住宅，但还不允许三拼住宅。

cues.en: And even better legislation means that Portland can once again build housing that used to be considered normal, such as fourplexes and cottage courts, which are several small homes around a common yard.
cues.zh: 更棒的立法意味着，波特兰又能建造过去被视为正常的住宅，比如四拼住宅和小屋庭院——也就是围绕共同院子的几栋小住宅。

cues.en: These cities are taking a good step forward, but they're still very much in the minority.
cues.zh: 这些城市迈出了不错的一步，但仍然是极少数。

cues.en: And unfortunately, other regulations, such as setbacks,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，其他法规，比如建筑退线、

cues.en: lot coverage rules,
cues.zh: 地块覆盖率规定、

cues.en: or minimum parking requirements can still make it difficult to build anything other than single family homes.
cues.zh: 或者最低停车位要求，仍然会让除独栋住宅以外的任何建筑都很难建起来。

cues.en: Also, even with these zoning changes, there are still far too many dense but livable housing options that are not permitted, such as courtyard buildings, townhouses,
cues.zh: 而且，即使有了这些分区改革，仍有太多高密度但宜居的住房类型不被允许，比如庭院式建筑、联排住宅、

cues.en: and small apartment buildings.
cues.zh: 以及小型公寓楼。

cues.en: Ultimately,
cues.zh: 归根结底，

cues.en: if US and Canadian cities want to succeed, they're going to have to start undoing car centric housing policy.
cues.zh: 如果美国和加拿大的城市想要成功，就必须开始废除以汽车为中心的住房政策。

cues.en: And ending single family zoning to make the missing middle legal again is a good first step.
cues.zh: 而终结独栋住宅分区、让“缺失的中间”重新合法化，是个好的第一步。

cues.en: And then they can start to bring back the enjoyable, walkable neighborhoods they used to build without having to live in a concrete box in the sky.
cues.zh: 然后他们就能开始重建过去那种宜人、适合步行的社区，而不必住在天上的混凝土盒子里。

cues.en: I'd
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: like to thank my supporters on Patreon who pay me to film random people's houses.
cues.zh: 想感谢我在 Patreon 上的支持者，他们付钱让我去拍陌生人的房子。

cues.en: If you'd like to support the channel and get access to bonus videos, visit patreon.com/notjustbikes.
cues.zh: 如果你想支持本频道并观看额外视频，请访问 patreon.com/notjustbikes。
